# 2020A Question 2 {.unnumbered}

::: {.exam-question}
## Question {.question-label}

[**Compare and contrast**]{.task-verb} povidone iodine and alcoholic chlorhexidine as skin antiseptic agents.
:::

:::: {#answer-structure}

## Suggested Structure

[**Compare and contrast**]{.task-verb} the agents in parallel columns, linking composition and mechanism to antimicrobial activity, onset, persistence, efficacy and adverse effects.

::: {.structure-table}
| Feature | Povidone Iodine | Alcoholic Chlorhexidine |
|---|---|---|
| Composition and Mechanism | | |
| Antimicrobial Spectrum and Resistance | | |
| Onset, Duration and Inactivation | | |
| Clinical Efficacy | | |
| Toxicity, Allergy and Flammability | | |
:::

::::

## Examiner Comments

::: {.examiner-comments}
This question was asking about two commonly used peri-operative antiseptic agents. The domains covered were similar to most previously asked pharmacology questions and covered physicochemistry, action, activity and adverse effects. This paper displayed a lack of knowledge of these two substances in the majority of candidates. A useful reference for this material would be in Katzung “Basic and Clinical Pharmacology” or Stoelting “Pharmacology and Physiology in Anesthetic Practice”.
:::
